claims.text: Pulse oximetry and chest x-ray with dyspnea or hemoptysis, or when pneumonia or other lung parenchymal disease is likely.
claims.quote: Pulse oximetry and chest radiograph should be performed in patients with red flag findings of dyspnea or hemoptysis and patients in whom suspicion of pneumonia or other parenchymal lung disease is high.

claims.text: Chest x-ray plus TB and HIV testing with weight loss or risk factors for those infections.
claims.quote: A chest radiograph and testing for TB and HIV infection should be performed in patients with weight loss or risk factors for those infections.

claims.text: No testing is needed for many patients without red flags; diagnose from history and exam and treat.
claims.quote: For many patients without red flag findings, clinicians can base the diagnosis on history and physical examination findings and begin treatment without testing.

claims.text: A good response to empiric treatment (for postnasal drip, airway hyperreactivity or GERD) usually makes further evaluation unnecessary.
claims.quote: An adequate clinical response to these interventions usually precludes the need for further evaluation.

claims.text: Chronic cough that doesn't respond: chest x-ray; if normal, test for asthma (spirometry, methacholine challenge if spirometry is normal), sinus disease (sinus CT) and GERD (esophageal pH monitoring).
claims.quote: Chest radiography should be performed in patients with chronic cough in whom presumptive treatment is ineffective. If the radiograph findings are unremarkable, many clinicians sequentially test for asthma (pulmonary function tests with methacholine challenge if standard spirometry is normal), sinus disease (sinus CT), and gastroesophageal reflux disease (esophageal pH monitoring).

claims.text: Sputum culture for possible indolent infection such as pertussis, TB or nontuberculous mycobacteria.
claims.quote: Sputum culture is helpful for patients with a possible indolent infection, such as pertussis, TB, or nontuberculous mycobacterial infection.

claims.text: Chest CT, possibly bronchoscopy, when lung cancer is suspected (eg, long smoking history) or empiric therapy has failed with inconclusive testing.
claims.quote: Chest CT and possibly bronchoscopy should be performed in patients in whom lung cancer or another bronchial tumor is suspected (eg, patients with a long smoking history, nonspecific constitutional signs) and in patients in whom empiric therapy has failed and who have inconclusive findings on preliminary testing.
